propositions: The completion verifier returns contradictory verdicts (PASS, FAIL, PASS) on identical inputs across multiple runs minutes apart with no code changes, making the close gate unreliable in both directions: spuriously blocking complete work (flaky FAILs) and spuriously passing incomplete work (flaky PASSes).

The verifier's non-determinism is concentrated on test-existence judgments where the LLM agent uses variable free-form search strategies (semantic/regex queries instead of literal substring and ticket-id lookup), causing it to inconsistently fail to locate tests that do exist in the tree.

The COMPLETION_VERDICT sidecar payload lacks the verified-at-sha, trace-id, and input-context metadata needed to prove non-determinism from stored data alone, making it impossible to distinguish input drift from genuine sampling variance post-hoc.

Unpinned LLM temperature allows sampling variance to flip borderline criteria verdicts; pinning temperature to 0 (greedy decoding) mirrors the plan-review verifier's existing mitigation and reduces variance-driven flips.

The completion verifier's prompt and agent configuration do not adequately direct the LLM to use literal-substring search-files calls and ticket-id / symbol lookups, and do not forbid drawing conclusions of test absence from failed semantic queries.
